sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry confirmed FLAG and IL-13Rα2 surface expression after sorting; no IL-13 binding or downstream signaling assay reported in this clip.
sites.rationale: IL-13Rα2 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with a signal peptide spanning residues 1–26 and a large extracellular domain from residue 27 to 343. The paper describes an 'N-terminal Flag tag' on the full-length, membrane-anchored protein; for a type I TM protein with a signal peptide, the only extracellular N-terminus is immediately after SP cleavage (after residue 26, before residue 27-D). Python-verified: seq[25]='S' (residue 26) and seq[26]='D' (residue 27), placing the tag junction 317 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. No specific residue number is named in the paper, so position is topology-derived rather than validated. Full-length human IL-13Rα2 stably expressed in U87 MG cells with an N-terminal FLAG tag (plus FLuc via IRES); cells sorted for FLAG and IL-13Rα2 surface expression by flow cytometry confirming surface display of the tagged construct.

sources.claim: HEK293T (CRL-3216) and Clone E6-1 Jurkat (TIB-152) lines were purchased from American Type Culture Collection (ATCC), while the U87 MG (HTB-14) line was generously gifted by Professor Forest White’s laboratory and transduced to stably express human IL-13Rα2 with an N-terminal Flag tag along with firefly luciferase (FLuc) via an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) sequence, then sorted for Flag and IL-13Rα2 expression to produce the IL-13Rα2 + U87 cell line ( online supplemental figure 4F ).

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It supports a single N-terminal FLAG tag site at the mature N-terminus of IL-13Rα2 (after signal peptide cleavage at residue 26). The paper confirms surface display by flow cytometry but reports no functional assay (e.g., IL-13 binding, STAT6 signaling) in the cited clip, so validation_level is surface_only. No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or intracellular positions are reported in the ledger.
